newsitem.title: USA: Pediatricians say drug labels are inadequate.
newsitem.headline: Pediatricians say drug labels are inadequate.

text.p: A leading doctor's group said Monday drug labels were not specific enough, noting that ingredients such as sweeteners and dyes have been known to trigger seizures, breathing problems and diarrhea.

The American Academy of Pediatrics policy statement said companies were not required to disclose inactive ingredients on the labels of drugs taken orally. Such substances were rarely named because manufacturers wanted to preserve "trade secret" fragrances and flavorings.

"The voluntary system is clearly inadequate," a report in the journal Pediatrics said. It recommended mandatory labeling of inactive ingredients on prescription and over-the-counter pharmaceutical products.
The group said the most common adverse reactions seen in children were seizures, headaches, bronchospasms, and diarrhea.

A recent survey of 102 chewable and liquid pediatric pharmaceuticals found 90 percent reported on the label that a sweetener was included but few provided the specific sweetener ingredient, the report said.
